meta.title: Year 8 Python and connected systems
meta.route: Python first, then Raspberry Pi Pico MicroPython in Wokwi; full Raspberry Pi computer concepts and hardware where available.
meta.next: Week 6 is ready: Build the memory-game lights. Use a ready-wired Pico in Wokwi; build from the lists and range loops taught in class. Binary/image objectives remain to be checked.
meta.intro: Students keep building confidence in Python, then use the same ideas to control a simulated device. They develop functions, data handling, 3D design and system testing before the major physical project.

weeks.title: Rules that work for people
weeks.learn: Decomposition, flowcharts and decisions with competing needs.
weeks.make: Retain actual earlier rule/design work; do not assume Python functions were already taught.
weeks.evidence: A traced rule and explanation of a design choice.

weeks.title: Can we trust this record
weeks.learn: Fields, types, units, source and time; missing is different from zero.
weeks.make: Use actual earlier data work or a short repair activity to establish the starting point.
weeks.evidence: A structured record with a justified correction.

weeks.title: Keep evidence you can explain
weeks.learn: Research, safe AI use, file versions and communicating a claim.
weeks.make: Retain the class work that was actually completed and collect missing evidence through later tasks.
weeks.evidence: Credited evidence and an organised working file.

weeks.title: Python game studio
weeks.learn: Variables, input/output, selection and repetition in a small game.
weeks.make: Keep the beginner Python game activity and stronger-student challenges already prepared.
weeks.evidence: A working program, a personal change and an explanation of a test.

weeks.title: Python lists and for loops
weeks.learn: Classroom teaching focused on Python lists and counted range loops.
weeks.make: Teacher-led replacement for the unsuccessful binary pixel lesson. Keep the original page as a revision resource, not proof of coverage.
weeks.evidence: Actual list/loop work from class. Bits, bytes and image representation remain unconfirmed.
weeks.status: taught: lists and loops; representation needs revisiting

weeks.title: Build the memory-game lights
weeks.learn: Lists, zero-based positions, counted range loops and len(); call a supplied hardware function.
weeks.make: Play a three-light pattern, choose a sequence for a partner and make the same loop handle different lengths.
weeks.evidence: Working Pico pattern player, short/long/repeated-item tests and an explanation of a list position.
weeks.status: prepared project; classroom outcome not yet checked

weeks.title: Make the memory game respond
weeks.learn: Digital button input and decisions; compare a response with a stored pattern.
weeks.make: Extend the working pattern player gradually. Start with one button and one comparison before a complete game.
weeks.evidence: Correct/wrong input tests and an individual explanation of the decision.

weeks.title: Beat the light
weeks.learn: Functions, elapsed time, input validation and repeatable tests.
weeks.make: Build a reaction-time game from a working button input. Reject early presses and keep several valid results.
weeks.evidence: Explained function, early/valid input tests and a usable results list.

weeks.title: Turn readings into useful evidence
weeks.learn: Lists/dictionaries, validation, CSV records, keys and a spreadsheet model.
weeks.make: Record source, units and status; link a small device table to readings and check a summary chart. Recorded/simulated data is sufficient.
weeks.evidence: Validated records, one checked lookup or query, formulas and a defensible conclusion.

weeks.title: Design a housing you can repair
weeks.learn: Dimensioned CAD, tolerances, assembly, access and alternative designs.
weeks.make: In Tinkercad 3D Design, model a repairable Pico enclosure with a removable lid. Check supplied component sizes and compare a fit allowance.
weeks.evidence: Two design choices, CAD views and a fit/access test.

weeks.title: Meet the Raspberry Pi computer
weeks.learn: A Linux single-board computer, OS, files, networks, client/server messages and GPIO.
weeks.make: Compare a full Raspberry Pi with Pico. Use a school Pi demonstration if available, or labelled system/file traces. Inspect a recorded JSON response and plan offline behaviour.
weeks.evidence: System/network diagram, interpreted record and an honest offline response.

weeks.title: Make your evidence understandable
weeks.learn: Accessible HTML/CSS, graphics, presentation and responsible AI-assisted communication.
weeks.make: Create a small device dashboard or explanation page using earlier readings; verify one AI-generated claim and improve the page after a user test.
weeks.evidence: Credited digital artefact, verified claim and a recorded accessibility improvement.

weeks.title: Connect the whole system
weeks.learn: Integrate a Python/MicroPython controller, structured data, CAD and a usable explanation.
weeks.make: Adapt earlier components for a chosen need. Distinguish the simulated device, data and physical build still required.
weeks.evidence: Independent function change, system test log and a justified design decision.

weeks.title: Demonstrate and improve

weeks.make: Change a function, diagnose a fault, check a data result and explain privacy/network choices. Recheck gaps before Christmas.

weeks.make: Turn the need into measurable targets and plan who will test them.
weeks.evidence: Year 7: five targets. Year 8: six targets with justified constraints.

weeks.title: Explore three possible solutions
weeks.learn: Sketch three concepts and compare usefulness, feasibility and impact.
weeks.make: Sketch three concepts and compare usefulness, feasibility and impact.

weeks.title: Model the design in 3D
weeks.learn: Develop CAD, dimensions, assembly and access before using materials.

weeks.make: Compare materials, joints, structures or mechanisms that matter to the chosen design.

weeks.learn: Transfer the autumn code and circuit into the project and isolate one fault at a time.

weeks.title: Make and assemble a physical prototype

weeks.make: Make the structure/housing and integrate controls, access and any necessary mechanism.

weeks.title: Find out where it fails

weeks.make: Test normal, boundary and failure conditions against the specification. Year 7 uses a structured test log; Year 8 justifies repeat counts and checks interactions between components.
weeks.evidence: Repeated results, a fault explanation and a ranked improvement.

weeks.title: Let someone else use it

weeks.make: Observe an approved user or peer using the prototype without coaching.

pico: New Raspberry Pi Pico MicroPython simulation
pi: Physical computing on a Raspberry Pi computer

sources: UNESCO AI competency framework for students
notes: 36 teaching weeks, two 40-minute periods per week; two additional 60-minute community sessions. Week numbers are teaching weeks and must be matched to local holidays.

The selected ICT toolkit is explicitly taught and checked before Christmas. January to April is the major D&T competition project. May starts a distinct exhibition brief; the final four teaching weeks focus on enterprise and fundraising.
Humans, Animals and Nature are represented across the class. Teams choose a bounded need from evidence; the whole autumn does not share a gardening theme.

Tinkercad Circuits supports Arduino text code in C++. Wokwi supports Pico with MicroPython. Pico is a microcontroller; it is not a simulation of a full Raspberry Pi running Linux. The Raspberry Pi Foundation online Python editor is a coding editor, not hardware simulation.

Begin simulations without assuming students own hardware. Before Christmas, CAD is a digital skill. During the D&T phases, schedule actual physical materials, making and testing; simulation alone does not demonstrate physical manufacture or real-world reliability.

Keep one main platform per year. Starter circuits and explained boilerplate reduce setup load; students must still make an independent change and explain it. Year 8 learns the differences between CPython, MicroPython machine.Pin and Raspberry Pi GPIO libraries before transferring code.

Learn defines new ideas from zero. Your turn contains building and testing. Quick reference uses coding-topic headings. Independent problems have meaningful constraints, rubric criteria and test evidence; Level up remains optional.

These are local selected outcomes informed by Cambridge, Pearson, England KS3 and IB design/ATL. They do not claim completion of several full programmes or use invented awarding-body objective codes. Detailed stage alignment needs the school’s licensed frameworks.
Use practical portfolio evidence and individual explanations. A prepared lesson is not evidence that a class has completed it. Competition placing and money raised are not assessment grades.
Confirm competition rules, deadline and equipment early in the spring project. If the event is later, complete a judged school demonstration by April and retain the entry package.

Year 9 direction for later agreement: applied AI and data, model evaluation/bias, automation and an independently managed impact project. AI literacy stays present in Years 7–8; specialist AI is a later progression, not a promise of a full Year 9 map here.
